description: A CLI tool for sharing knowledge files across projects via git-backed sources.
releaseNotes: GitHub releases include a native `eru-osx-arm64` binary for Apple Silicon, so `mise use github:dburriss/eru` and similar installers find a matching asset instead of falling back to the Rosetta-only `eru-osx-x64` A `brand` layout slot on the generated site: the logo in the nav is now markup (`brand-mark`, `brand-name` and `brand-cursor` spans) that `site.layout.brand` can replace with `html` or `text` items, or remove with `false`. `{{root}}` in the markup is the relative path back to the site root Footer `text` and `html` items on the generated site: `{ "text": "markdown" }` renders Markdown with raw HTML escaped, `{ "html": "raw" }` is emitted as is, and both accept `{ "file": "path" }` to read a repo-relative file (watched by `eru site serve`). They are footer-only Table views on the generated site have visible sort controls on every column header. Headers are keyboard-operable buttons that expose `aria-sort`, and sorting uses the same keys as the `sort` page option (dates, trust tiers, sync status) instead of the displayed text, with blank cells last Search can be limited to specific sources: `eru search --source ` (repeatable, `-s`) and a `sources` parameter on the `search_knowledge` MCP tool. Names match case-insensitively and any of them may match; `local` selects local `knowledge/` files. An unknown source name is an error that lists the valid ones `mcp.idleTimeoutMinutes` (and `ERU__MCP__IDLETIMEOUTMINUTES`) pauses an `eru mcp` server's background refresh after that many minutes without a request. The server keeps answering and the next request resumes it. `0`, the default, never pauses A plain local folder (not a git repo) can be a source: `eru source add ~/second-brain --scan`. The folder is read in place — nothing is cloned or copied into the cache, so `eru cache prune` and `eru cache clear` never touch it. Folder sources are OKF-only: markdown files under registered `okf` bundles are indexed, skipping dot-directories and `okf.ignorePatterns` directories. Sync stats the tree and re-reads only files whose modified time or size changed, and drops entries for files that were removed or renamed. A missing or unmounted folder keeps the old index and reports an error. `--branch`, `--basepath`, manifests and collections do not apply to folder sources `eru okf init --update` regenerates the catalog (folder list and concept table) of existing `index.md` files, so indexes no longer go stale. Catalogs now sit between `` and `` markers, and only that block is rewritten; prose around it is kept. `--force` (with `--update`) adopts indexes that have no markers yet: it replaces an eru-shaped table (and `## Folders` list), or appends a block. `--force` only touches genuine OKF indexes (inside a bundle whose root `index.md` has `okf_version`, index-shaped frontmatter, a folder with concepts or subfolders); foreign `index.md` files are skipped with the reason. Lone or duplicated markers are never rewritten. `eru okf fix` also refreshes marked indexes and lists unmarked ones as skipped `eru okf validate` warns with `missing-catalog-markers`, `stale-index` and `malformed-catalog-markers` for catalog indexes (warnings never change the exit code) Site themes follow the mocks more closely: filter values (row tags and sources) are bordered buttons, and they fill when their token is in the query line. The `source`/`status`/`tag` key button fills while its values are being completed. Both use a `q-on` class (and `aria-pressed` on the value buttons), which themes recolour. `smiley` now defaults to the cards view with a facet sidebar on Browse and fills orange, `cyberpunk` magenta and `ledger` with a soft tint. `ledger` now turns the query line off (its facet sidebar does the filtering) and keeps the plain search box; row tags and sources are plain links on a page with no query line, not dead filter buttons. The brand mark moved from CSS pseudo-elements to markup, so a `custom.css` that styles `.nav-brand::before` or `::after` should target `.brand-mark` and `.brand-cursor` **Breaking:** the sync-state glyph (`●`/`◐`/`○`) and badge no longer show in site listings by default. Set `site.showSyncStatus` to `true` (or `ERU__SITE__SHOWSYNCSTATUS=true`) to show them. The `sync:` filter and an explicit `syncStatus` table column are unchanged. **Breaking:** the `top` layout slot is renamed `nav`. A config that puts page ids or links in `top` now fails with a message pointing to `nav`; rename the key (also `ERU__SITE__LAYOUT__TOP__*` to `ERU__SITE__LAYOUT__NAV__*`). `top` is now a full-width widget band. **Breaking:** the `query` widget is no longer valid in `main`; it goes in `toolbar`, `left` or `right`. Browse now shows `title` in `top`, the query line in `toolbar` and `list` in `main`. **Breaking:** the generated site has a new terminal look: monospace type, square corners, hairline borders and an orange accent. The CSS variable names are unchanged, so a `custom.css` that sets `--color-*`, `--font-family` or `--radius` still applies, but overrides of component classes may need a second look. **Breaking:** Browse is now a query line above a table of name, source and tags, with no sidebar. Set `layout.left` to `["facets"]` to bring the sidebar back, or `defaultView` to `cards` for the old cards. `eru source disable ` and `eru source enable ` switch a source off and on without removing it. A disabled source is not synced, searched, served over MCP or shown in the site, and collection files pointing at it are skipped. It is also the `enabled` field of a source entry and `ERU__SOURCE____ENABLED`, and `eru source list` shows its status. `-g` edits the global config; otherwise a url-less local entry is used so only the current repo is affected. Site themes: `site.theme` (`terminal` by default, or `ledger`) switches the look of the generated site. A theme is a folder with a `theme.json` (default `site` settings) and a `theme.css`; custom themes go in `.eru/themes//` or `~/.config/eru/themes//`. Your config and `custom.css` still win. `ERU__SITE__THEME` and `eru config set site.theme` work too. See [themes](docs/reference/site-generation.md#themes). `eru theme list` shows the built-in and installed themes and which one is active. A `matrix` site theme: the terminal layout in phosphor green, with a faint glow and scanlines in dark mode. Select it with `eru config set site.theme matrix`. A `smiley` site theme: the terminal layout in blue and orange, with a blue header, sans-serif type and rounded pills. Select it with `eru config set site.theme smiley`. A `cyberpunk` site theme: the terminal layout in neon magenta, cyan and yellow, with a grid and glow in dark mode (pale lavender in light), angular display type and clipped corners. Select it with `eru config set site.theme cyberpunk`. A `rows` view: one bordered row per document with its description, source, tags and sync state. It is the `ledger` theme's default. New layout slots `top`, `toolbar` and `footer`: full-width bands above and below the columns. Every page footer links to the eru docs by default; set `footer` to replace it or `"footer": false` to remove it. Widgets are valid in more slots (`breadcrumbs`, `title`, `stale` in `top`; `meta`, `verified`, `generated`, `description`, `tags`, `cli`, `links` in `top` and `footer`). The query line can be moved: `query` is valid in `toolbar`, `left` and `right` (once per page), and any page can opt in. A `query` widget: type `tag:`, `source:` or `status:` to filter with a completion list and live counts, exclude with `-tag:x`, click a source or tag in the table to add it, and share the filtered view through `?q=` in the address. Press `/` to focus it and `j`, `k` and enter to move through rows. The sync state of each file shows as a glyph before its name (`●` pulled, `◐` cached, `○` index-only), and rows carry a `data-sync` attribute. Servers left running from an older install no longer undo newer state: an `eru mcp` started before an upgrade used to keep syncing with old code and overwrite `index.json` (for example back to 0 entries). `index.json` records the eru version that wrote it and an older eru refuses to overwrite it (the server logs that it is stale and stops syncing). Index writes are atomic, so a reader never sees a half-written file. Each server registers in `~/.cache/eru/mcp/` and exits when it finds a newer eru running; servers of the same version are left alone. Servers started before this change have no such check, so after upgrading stop them once with `pkill -f 'eru mcp'` and run `eru sync` Several `eru mcp` servers used to each run their own background sync. Now only one runs at a time across all `eru mcp` servers and `eru sync`: an exclusive lock on `~/.cache/eru/sync.lock` plus a throttle (a timer sync is skipped if another process synced less than half a refresh interval ago). `refresh_knowledge` bypasses the throttle but still waits for the lock; `eru sync` waits up to a minute and then reports that another sync is running A `--color-*` override under `:root` in `custom.css` now takes effect. The theme colours were set on `body`, which shadowed any `:root` rule; they now sit on `` with no extra specificity, and the theme class is stamped on both `` and ``. Per-theme overrides under `body.theme-light` and `body.theme-dark` keep working. A `pages.browse` override with a `table` block no longer needs `"view": "table"`. Browse renders as a table by default, but validation judged it as cards and rejected the block.
